newsitem.title: USA: Groups seek NAFTA probe on Canadian green law.
newsitem.headline: Groups seek NAFTA probe on Canadian green law.

text.p: An environmental group is planning to ask an international commission to begin an investigation to see if Canada is properly enforcing hydropower regulations, the Sierra Club said.

The petition, to be filed Wednesday by the group's legal defense fund, accuses Canada of breaking an environmental side agreement to the North American Free Trade Agreement by not clamping down on violations of laws designed to protect fish at hydropower dams.
According to the petition, British Columbia Hydro is producing power when water should be stored for salmon, and storing water at times when salmon need the flows for their spring migration.
At the same time, B.C. Hydro's northwestern U.S. competitors are being required to take steps to protect fish.

"B.C. Hydro is turning U.S. environmental regulations into a market opportunity at the overall expense of salmon runs in the Pacific Northwest," Patti Goldman, a Sierra Club Legal Defense Fund attorney, said in a statement.

NAFTA established an environmental panel to investigate whether parties to the agreement were weakening their green laws to gain an advantage over their trading partners in attracting or keeping investments.
To launch a investigation, two out of three environmental ministers from the United States, Canada and Mexico must accept a petition.

A spokesman for the U.S. National Marine Fisheries Service said the hydropower issue "isn't on anyone's frontburner. "Even if it were a truly hot issue, it would be hard to get any hearing since you have to have two of three ministers."
Canadian Embassy officials had no immediate comment on the petition.
